title: Pocket Connector manifest
description: A Pocket Connector: an MCP server exposing callable tools. Unlike a Skill — which is instructions loaded into context — a Connector is a running process the agent calls, so it declares transport, authentication and the tools it provides.

name.description: URL-safe identifier. Combined with the author handle it forms the connector's unique reference.

summary.description: What service this connects to and what it can do. Shown on the marketplace card, so it must stand alone without the README.

transport.description: How Pocket reaches the server. `stdio` is a local process and the most common; `http` and `sse` are hosted endpoints.

auth.description: How the connector authenticates. `none` for public or local-only, `apiKey` for a single shared secret, `oauth2` when each user authorises individually.

scopes.description: Permissions the connector needs. Must be empty when auth is `none` — there is nothing to scope without authentication. Keep these minimal: they are shown to the user at install time, and a connector asking for more than it uses will not be trusted.

endpoint.description: The base URL, for `http` and `sse` transports. Must be HTTPS.

command.description: How to start the server, for the `stdio` transport.

tools.description: Every tool this connector exposes. Agents choose a tool by reading its description, so each one must say precisely what it does and does not do — a vague description gets the wrong tool called.

name.description: Verb-first and snake_case, e.g. `create_issue` rather than `issues` — the agent reasons about the name, so it should read as an action.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema for the tool's parameters. This is what the model fills in, so describe every property — an undescribed field gets guessed at.

readOnly.description: True when the tool only reads. Lets Pocket run it without the confirmation a mutating call needs.

allOf.description: A local process needs a command to start it.
